issues.text: The correction of misconception 1 ends by saying the declared type shows it. The type only shows that no rows exist yet at .Where(...); it does not show that the later .ToListAsync() filters in PostgreSQL rather than loading everything and filtering in C#. The earlier part of the correction (one SQL statement with WHERE) carries the point; this last sentence overclaims.
issues.quote: You notice this in the declared type: until `.ToListAsync()` you hold an `IQueryable<Order>`, a description, never a list of rows that C# could filter.
issues.fix: Narrow the sentence to what the type shows: 'You notice the first half in the declared type: until .ToListAsync() you hold an IQueryable<Order>, not rows; the WHERE itself travels in the one SQL statement.'

issues.text: The FindAsync paragraph packs three ideas (FirstOrDefaultAsync taking a condition, Items joined from order_items, one row per item reassembled into one Order) into one block; I had to re-read it twice to see why 'first' means the first order.
issues.quote: That JOIN returns one row per item, each repeating the order's columns; EF Core assembles those rows into one `Order` whose `Items` holds all of them, so "first" means the first order, not its first item.
issues.fix: Split the paragraph after 'one SQL statement.' so the one-row-per-item sentence stands as its own short paragraph.

issues.text: q2's explanation refers to 'section 5', but the lesson's headings are not numbered; the reader has to count headings to find it.
issues.fix: Replace 'section 5' with the heading name: 'As "In the Đơn Hàng system" explains for FindAsync' (en, vi).

issues.text: q6: the lesson never discusses speed, so I picked d by eliminating a, b, c (each contradicts the lesson), not by understanding 'speed can't show where filtering happens'. Explanation b adds a new idea (C#-side filtering would be slower) the lesson never establishes.
issues.quote: and filtering in C# would have to load every row first, which is slower, not faster, on a customer with many orders.
issues.fix: Drop the 'slower, not faster' clause from explanation b, keeping only that speed alone proves nothing and the WHERE runs in PostgreSQL (en, vi).
